name: Plastic
summary: Bottles, tubs, and rigid plastic that is empty, clean, and dry.
tips: Keep lids together when your city accepts them
caution: Soft film and multilayer wrappers often need a special drop-off.

name: Paper & Cardboard
summary: Clean paper, office sheets, boxes, and cartons.
caution: A little food or liquid can contaminate an entire paper load.

name: Glass
summary: Glass jars and bottles are valuable when empty and separated.
caution: Ceramics, mirrors, and heat-resistant glass are different materials.

name: Metal
summary: Steel and aluminium cans, tins, and clean foil.
tips: Bundle small foil into a ball
caution: Paint tins and aerosol cans may need special handling.

name: Organic / Wet
summary: Food scraps and other compostable kitchen waste.
tips: Use a compostable liner if accepted
caution: Compostable packaging belongs here only where your local program accepts it.

name: E-waste
summary: Phones, chargers, cables, batteries, and electronics.
tips: Never burn or dismantle at home
caution: Lithium batteries can cause fires when mixed with regular bins.

name: Hazardous
summary: Chemicals, paint, bulbs, and pressurised containers.

name: Textiles
summary: Clothes, shoes, linens, and fabric items.
caution: Wet or mouldy textiles can make reuse impossible.

name: Medical
summary: Medicines, sharps, test strips, and clinical waste.
caution: Medical waste should never go into household recycling.
